### Rating the Quality of Available Budget Information

The accessibility, transparency, and format (i.e. how easy the source data is for citizens to use) of budget information can vary considerably between government entities.  I've attempted to create a clear rubric for scoring the quality of available budget information to both give people an idea of how easy or difficult it may be for them to use these data, as well as to be able to point out easy changes that local government entities could make to improve the quality of the budget information they make publicly available.

<details>
<summary style="font-size: 1.25em;">Rubric</summary>

Each publicly available budget is scored from 0 to 2 on its Accessibility, Transparency, and Format.  The minimum possible score is 0, indicating the lowest quality budget information. The maximum possible score is 6, indicating the highest quality budget information. 

<div style="width:700px; margin:0 auto;">

#### Accessibility

<table style="text-align: center; background-color: #EEE;"><thead>
  <tr>
    <th width="100px">Score</th>
    <th width="500px">Description</th>
  </tr></thead>
<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>0</td>
    <td>Not Available online</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>1</td>
    <td>Available online</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>2</td>
    <td>Easily found via search engines</td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<br/>


#### Transparency

<table style="text-align: center; background-color: #EEE;"><thead>
  <tr>
    <th width="100px">Score</th>
    <th width="500px">Description</th>
  </tr></thead>
<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>0</td>
    <td>Documents only overall revenue and expenses</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>1</td>
    <td>Includes budgetary detail at the function/department level</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>2</td>
    <td>Includes budgetary detail within functions/departments</td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<br/>

#### Format

<table style="text-align: center; background-color: #EEE;"><thead>
  <tr>
    <th width="100px">Score</th>
    <th width="500px">Description</th>
  </tr></thead>
<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>0</td>
    <td>Available as image-only PDFs (can't search text) or as webpage objects</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>1</td>
    <td>Available as text searchable PDFs (OCR or True PDF)</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>2</td>
    <td>Available as tabular data (json, .csv, .xlsx, etc.)</td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</div>

</details>

## Budget Information By Entity

<hr>

Budget Information Quality Scores and direct sources (e.g. links to pdf downloads or websites containing budget information) are presented for each major governmental entity in Kendall county.

<br/>

### Kendall County


<details>
<summary style="font-size: 1.25em;">Budget Information Quality <span style="background-color: #98FB98;"> **5/6** </span></summary>

- **2/2** - Accessibility
	- *Direct link to budgets returned as second result for Google search term "Kendall County Texas budget"*
- **2/2** - Transparency
	- *Very detailed and comprehensive information by department*
- **1/2** - Format
	- *Well formatted text-searchable pdf*

</details>

### City of Boerne


<details>
<summary style="font-size: 1.25em;">Budget Information Quality <span style="background-color: #FEF569;"> **4/6** </span></summary>

- **2/2** - Accessibility
	- *Direct link to budgets returned as top result for Google search term "City of Boerne budget"*
- **2/2** - Transparency
	- *Detailed information by department available through web application*
- **0/2** - Format
	- *No available direct download. Web application is intuitive and well-designed, but is intended for web-based viewing only. Not intuitively, the web application includes a 'print' button that brings up a menu to select areas of the budget you would like to download, then asks for an email address to send you a link. I submitted a request for a link using this method, but never received a link so I could download the report.*

</details>
